note: The engine this plugin runs bash on. Built from source at a pinned upstream commit plus this repository patch set, because four behaviours this plugin's contract depends on are not upstream: a pattern/script/program word is never rewritten into its Win32 spelling, a shell may ask for a named file command to be run from PATH instead of the engine's in-process copy, a shell-side pipeline producer does not deadlock against the last member's undrained output pipe, and a cd into /tmp leaves the shell where pwd says it is. `ref` is a commit because a tag can be moved; `tag` records the release it was cut from. `artifact` is the build shipped inside this package: `scripts/build-engine.mjs --refresh` replaces it and rewrites the hash. The hash is the provenance of the shipped bytes, not a reproducible-build promise: replaying the pin and the patches rebuilds the same code but not the same file, so a rebuilt engine is verified behaviourally, by `npm test` and the corpus, never by comparing hashes.
why: rubash is a from-scratch bash 5.3 engine whose own test surface is the GNU upstream suite, so almost everything this repository used to patch (a real PID behind $!, /tmp as an alias, descriptor paths, kill as a builtin, CRLF scripts, select, nameref, read -t) is correct upstream. The one behaviour still missing is the data-primary rule above, which only the WinuxCmd suite gets; patch 0001 extends it to every child class. Patch 0002 drops an environment entry Unicode cannot carry instead of aborting before the first command. Patch 0003 adds RUBASH_FILE_COMMANDS_FROM_PATH, which is how this plugin sends sed and rmdir to its toolchain's programs: the in-process copies of those two disagree with GNU (no \b, \{m,n\} or \| in the matcher; rmdir accepts a final dot and swallows every error), and the command runs in the inline pipeline path as well as the plain one. Patch 0004 starts the last pipeline member's output drains before the shell-side producer runs: 1.4.3 ran that producer to completion first, so a streaming consumer that filled its own 64 KiB output pipe stopped reading, blocked the producer, and left nobody to start the drain. Patch 0005 makes cd into a virtual root that has a real directory behind it (/tmp, /home) move the process as well: the logical-only bridge rewrote PWD and stopped, so every relative operand and every child process stayed in the previous directory while pwd reported the new one.
